Title: Protection of Private Forests Regulations, 1968 (L.N. No. 343 of 1968).
Abstract: The 9 regulations carry the following titles: Issuing Authority (1); Short Title (2); Definitions (3); Precautions Regarding the Kindling of Fires (4); Fire Extinguishing (5); Forest Insects and Diseases (6); Other Threatening Damages (7); Penal (8); Effective date (9).
Keywords: forest management/forest conservation; private forest; forest fires; offences/penalties; hazards

Title: Forest and Wildlife Conservation and Development Proclamation (No. 192/1980).
Abstract: The 26 sections of this Proclamation are divided into three Parts: General (I); Forest and Wildlife Conservation and Development Authority (II); Miscellaneous Provisions (III). There is hereby established a Forest and Wildlife Conservation and Development Authority (hereinafter the Authority) having its own juridical personality. The Authority shall, among other tasks, establish and administer national parks, game reserves and other conservation areas. Within the Authority a Forest and Wildlife Conservation and Development Council shall be established. No person, unless he is in possession of a written permission from the Authority, may: a) hunt wild animals or use the products thereof; b) settle in any state forest, national park, game reserve, or other conservation area; c) fell trees, collect, load or transport any state forest product; d) graze cattle in any forest, national park, game reserve, or other conservation area or commit any other act detrimental thereto.
Keywords: protected area; basic legislation; institution; governance

Title: Protection of State Forests Regulations, 1968 (L. N. 344 of 1968).
Abstract: The 8 regulations carry the following Titles: Issuing Authority (1); Short Title (2); Definitions (3); Precautions Regarding the Kindling of Fires (4); Fire Extinguishing (5); Other Treathening Damages, Including Grazing (6); Penal (7); Effective Date (8).
Keywords: forest management/forest conservation; public forest; forest fires; offences/penalties; hazards

Title: Exploitation of State Forests Regulations, 1968 (L. N. No. 345 of 1968).
Abstract: The 10 regulations carry the following titles: Issuing Authority (1); Short Title (2); Definitions (3); Forest Operation Plan (4); Marking the Trees for Cutting (5); Methods of Exploitation (6); Marketing (7); Rules for Auction or Tender (8); Penal (9); Effective Date (10). No state forest shall be exploited unless in conformity with an operation plan or in exceptional cases with a preliminary working scheme (Reg. 4). Exploitation can only be carried out by: a) the Ministry; b) villagers and local inhabitants entitled to purchase products under paragraph 2 of article 6; and c) concessionaires in accordance with paragraph 3, article 6.
Keywords: public forest; private forest; timber extraction/logging; policy/planning; internal trade; offences/penalties; forest management/forest conservation

Title: Exploitation of Private Forest Regulations (L. N. No. 346 of 1968).
Abstract: The 13 regulations carry the following titles: Issuing Authority (1); Short Title (2); Definitions (3); Application for Forest Exploitation Permit (4); Operation Plan (5); Obligation to Reforest (6); Exploitation Permit (7); Marking of Trees for Cutting (8); Marketing (9); Inspection of Cutting Operations (10); Records (11); Penal (12); Effective Date (13).
Keywords: private forest; policy/planning; afforestation/reforestation; timber extraction/logging; offences/penalties; forest management/forest conservation

Title: Management of Protective Forests Regulations, 1968 (L. N. No. 347 of 1968).
Abstract: The 9 regulations carry the following titles: Issuing Authority (1); Short Title (2); Definitions (3); Management Plan (4); Utilization (5); Marketing (6); Afforestation (7); Penal (8); Effective Date (9). Protective forests can be public or privately owned forests. Rules of these Regulations apply equally both, except that a private owner shall bear expenses of afforestation of private land, whereas afforestation of public land shall be paid for by the Government (reg. 7).
Keywords: protection forest; forest management/forest conservation; policy/planning; timber extraction/logging; public forest; private forest

Title: Powers of Rangers Regulation, 1968 (L. N. No. 349 of 1968).
Abstract: The 8 regulations carry the following titles: Issuing Authority (1); Short Title (2); Definitions (3); Establishment of Forest Ranger Service (4); Duties and Powers of Forest Rangers (5); Uniforms and Arms (6); Penal (7); Effective Date (8). These Regulations provide for the establishment of a Forest Ranger Service for the protection of forests and the implementation of forestry laws and regulations.
Keywords: public forest; forest service; forest management/forest conservation

Title: Powers of Forest Guards Regulations, 1968 (L. N. 350 of 1968).
Abstract: The 9 regulations carry the follwing titles: Issuing Authority (1); Short Title (2); Definitions (3); Establishment of Forest Guard Service (4); Duties of Forest Guards (5); Steps to be Taken by Forest Guards (6); Uniforms and Arms (7); Penal (8); Effective Date (9). Forest Guards shall: (a) protect and guard state forests; (b) ensure handling or use of forest products from state and private forests; and (c) ensure implementation of forest laws. (9 regulations)
Keywords: public forest; private forest; forest service; offences/penalties; forest management/forest conservation

Title: Trade of Saw Logs and Veneer Logs Regulations, 1968 (L. N. No. 351 of 1968).
Abstract: The 6 regulations carry the following titles: Issuing Authority (1); Short Title (2); Definitions (3); Report (4); Penal (5); Effective Date (6). Every Person operating a sawmill, veneer mill, plywood factory, or any plant processing forest products, whether from a state forest or private forest shall annually report on the ownership of the plant and location, capacity and mechanical description of the plant in the form as reproduced in the Annex.
Keywords: internal trade; processing/handling; data collection/reporting

Title: Government Ownership of Urban Lands and Extra Houses Proclamation No. 47/1975.
Abstract: The Proclamation is divided into 7 Chapters: Introduction (I); Urban Lands (II); Urban Houses (III); Rent (IV); Cooperative Societies of Urban Dwellers (V); Powers and Duties of the Ministry (VI); General Provisions (VII). The Proclamation vests all urban lands in the Government (sect. 3).
Keywords: land tenure; urban land; public land; institution; governance

Title: Public Ownership of Rural Lands Proclamation No. 31/1975.
Abstract: The Proclamation is divided into 6 Chapters: Introduction (1); Public Ownership of Rural Lands (2); Establishment of Associations for the Implementation of the Proclamation (3); Powers and Functions of the Minister of Land Reform and Administration (4); Communal and Nomadic Lands (5); General Provisions (6). The Proclamation declares all rural lands to be the collective property of the Ethiopian people and abolishes private ownership of rural land (sect. 3). Peasant Associations are in charge of the redistribution, cultivation, administration etc. of rural lands.
Keywords: agricultural land; land reform; land tenure; traditional rights/customary rights; institution; non-governmental entity; ownership; smallholders/peasants; common property; community management; governance; property rights; water rights

Title: Peasant Associations Consolidation Proclamation No. 223/1982.
Abstract: The Proclamation regulates the following matters: objectives, powers and duties of Peasant Associations, organization and method of work of Peasant Associations, membership; rights and duties of members. Further provisions regard the Kebele Peasant Association; Provincial, Awraja and Woreda Peasant Associations, and all Ethiopian Peasant associations. Moreover, the Proclamation deals with judicial tribunals, the Revolution Defence Committee and the Permanent Secretariat.
Keywords: agricultural land; non-governmental entity; cooperative/producer organization; agricultural development; smallholders/peasants

Title: Valleys Agricultural Development Authority Establishment Proclamation No. 118/1977.
Abstract: The Proclamation establishes the Valleys Agricultural Development Authority. Its principal objective shall be to coordinate, regulate and supervise the development and utilization of land and water resources of river valleys for agricultural development (sect. 6).
Keywords: agricultural development; institution; governance

Title: Plant Quarantine Council of Ministers Regulation No. 4/1992.
Abstract: All imported plants and other articles which are infested or infected with plant pests are subject to plant quarantine. Plants and articles as specified in Schedule I require an import permit (art. 4). The importation of any plant or other article specified in Schedule II is prohibited (art. 5). Plants listed in Schedule I need a phytosanitary certificate when imported (art. 6). Exported plants shall be accompanied by a phytosanitary certificate only of required by the importing country. The Inspector may waive any or all conditions relating to plant quarantine (art. 7). Article 10 provides for quarantine stations. The remaining articles outline powers and responsibilities of Inspectors and powers of the Minister with respect to prevention of the spreading of diseases and pests, the establishment of new quarantine stations and amendment of the Schedules. (15 articles completed by 3 Schedules)
Keywords: quarantine; pests/diseases; inspection; plant protection

Title: Urban Lands Lease Holding Proclamation No. 80/1993.
Abstract: A Proclamation to provide for the utilization of urban land. Urban land is defined as all land within the boundaries of a town (sect. 2). The Proclamation shall not apply to land previously utilized for the construction of dwellings (sect. 3). Section 4 provides for applications of persons who desire to hold urban land in lease. Such applications shall be submitted to the town administration. The town administration shall issue the leaseholding permit and a title document in accordance with provisions city master plans or, where such a plan does not exist, in accordance with regional self-government directions. Also shall the permit be subject to competitive public tendering (sects. 5 and 6). Section 7 pescribes the duration of leases in various areas. The rates of rent shall be determined by a law issued by the appropriate national/regional council (sect. 8). Section 10 makes provision for the transfer of mortgage of use rights, section 11 for the termination of lease agreements. (17 sections)
Keywords: land tenure; urban land; lease; authorization/permit; contracts

Title: Maritime Proclamation No. 137 of 1953.
Abstract: These Parts of the Marine Proclamation relate to jurisdiction, administration and control of territorial waters, maritime domain and defence areas of the Empire and fishing rights in those waters. Rights of fishing of foreigners are limited to (restricted) pearl fishing (sect. 9).
Keywords: marine fisheries; registration; foreign fishing; enforcement/compliance; maritime zone; territorial sea; sovereignty; maritime boundaries

Title: Water Resources Utilization Proclamation No. 92/1994.
Abstract: This Proclamation regulates the use of water resources, by requiring a government permit in respect of most water uses, with the exception of minor and traditional uses (art. 3). The Proclamation further lays down basic criteria for the permit-granting authorities to use in deciding on applications for permits (art. 5). Permits are subject to a term of duration, renewable on expiration (art. 6), and can be varied, suspended, revoked, and transferred, under the circumstances indicated by the statute (arts. 7 and 8). In particular, the Government has authority to vary a permit, subject to compensating the affected permit holder (art. 7.3). Payment of water permit fees and water charges, and the recording of permits in water registers, are also provided for (arts. 10 and 11.4, respectively). The permit granting Government authority also serves as judge of first instance in disputes between permit holders or between a permit holder and another party, concerning rights and obligations under a water utilization permit (art. 13).
Keywords: basic legislation; water rights; authorization/permit; dispute settlement; servitude; water supply; irrigation; legal proceedings/administrative proceedings

Title: Forestry Conservation, Development and Utilization Proclamation No. 94/1994.
Abstract: The 18 sections of this Proclamation are divided into 4 Parts: General (I); Conservation and development of forests (II); Utilization of forests (III); Miscellaneous provisions (IV). There shall be three types of forests: State forests, Regional Forests, and Private Forests. A State Forests is a forest designated as such by the Council of Ministers for purposes of protection of genetic resources and the eco-system. A Regional Forest shall be designated as such by a Region. Section 7 provides for the designation of any forest as a protected forest by the Ministry of Natural Resources Development and Environment protection or an appropriate regional body. The Ministry shall designate, demarcate and register state and protected forests and establish a central forestry register (sect. 4). Section 6 prescribes duties of owners with respect to the conservation and development of private forests. State and regional forests shall be utilized in accordance with management plans either approved by the Ministry or the appropriate regional body (sect. 9). Part IV provides, inter alia, for transport and storage of forest products, prohibits certain activities in state and regional forests, and defines powers and duties of forests guards.
Keywords: basic legislation; forest management/forest conservation; private forest; public forest; protected area; forest service; offences/penalties

Title: Agricultural Cooperative Societies Proclamation No. 85/1994.
Abstract: A society established under this Proclamation shall have as objectives: (1) to improve the living conditions of its members; (2) to promote self-reliance among members; (3) to solve problems collectively; (4) to obtain modern technologies for its members; (5) to process agricultural products; (6) to promote teaching and training for its members (sect. 3). Provisions of Part II, concerning the formation and registration of societies, distinguish between a Primary Society and a Higher Level Society. A Primary Society shall be established on a voluntary basis by not less than ten peasants living in a given area (sect. 5). A Higher Level Society is a union or federation of Primary Societies (sects. 6-8). The field or area in which a Society may engage shall be determined in its By-laws (sect. 7). Any society shall be registered by the appropriate authority (sect. 9). Provisions of Part III describe the rights and duties of Societies and its members. Other provisions of this Proclamation deal with internal procedures, special privileges of societies, funds and properties as well as the winding up of societies. The Proclamation consists of 48 sections and which are divided into 8 Parts.
Keywords: cooperative/producer organization; basic legislation; agricultural development; capacity building; education; smallholders/peasants

Title: Ethiopian Valleys Development Studies Authority Establishment Proclamation No. 318/1977.
Abstract: Valley means a boundary to be designated as such by the Authority in accordance with article 6(1). The Valleys shall be delimited on the basis of water flows. Article 3 provides for the establishment of the Authority and article 5 defines the objectives of this institution: (1) to conduct studies and research of natural resources; (2) prepare development master plans for valleys; (3) conduct studies and research for the protection of the environment; (4) conduct studies and research pertaining to transboundary rivers. The Authority shall, inter alia, identify development projects and conduct feasibility studies of irrigation projects (art. 6). The Authority shall be guided by a Council consisting mainly of representatives of various ministries (art. 8). The remaining provisions define powers and duties of the General Manager and Deputy General Manager and the Council.
Keywords: institution; agricultural development; water resources management; policy/planning; research; basin/catchment/watershed; sustainable development; irrigation; transboundary waters; inland waters; governance

Title: Ethiopian Agricultural Research Organization Proclamation No. 79/1997.
Abstract: This Proclamation provides for the establishment of the Ethiopian Agricultural Research Organization as an autonomous Government body. This Institute shall coordinate agricultural research activity and build up a research capacity of its own (art. 5). Agricultural research means research aiming at improving the production and productivity of plants, animals and natural resources. Natural resources is defined as soil, forest, including water related to agriculture. Powers of the Organization are outlined in detail in article 6. The structure of the Organization shall include a Research Board, a Director-General and agricultural research centres established or to be established by the Federal Government (art. 7).
Keywords: institution; agricultural development; research; governance

Title: Proclamation on radiation protection (No. 79/1993).
Abstract: The provisions of this Proclamation shall be applicable to all sources of ionising radiation above the exemption level (sect. 1). There is hereby established a National Radiation Protection Authority as an autonomous public authority having its own legal personality. The Authority shall be accountable to the Ethiopian Science and Technology Commission. The objectives of the Authority shall be: to render radiation protection services; to regulate, control and supervise radiological work and all activities relating to the acquisition, use, transportation and disposal of radioactive substances, x-ray equipment and other machines capable of emitting ionising radiation; and to promote and encourage research and development in radiation protection. The Authority shall formulate radiation protection policies and submit to the government for approval; issue guidelines, rules, and directives for the implementation of policies concerning radiation protection and follow up their implementation, and have licensing and other powers in the field of radiation protection (sect. 7). Within the Authority a Radiation Protection Board shall be established and a Chief Radiation Protection Officer appointed. The importation, exportation, manufacture, possession, sale, use, storage, transportation or disposal of radioactive materials or devices emitting ionising radiation shall only be based on licenses issued by the Authority (sect. 17). Duties and responsibilities of license holders and other concerned parties are described in section 21. (28 sections)
Keywords: pollution control; radiation; emissions; food safety and quality; treated food; radiation

Title: Marine Transport Proclamation No. 139/1978.
Abstract: There is hereby established a Marine Transport Authority (hereinafter the Authority) as an autonomous public authority having juridical personality. Purposes of the Authority are set out in section 6 and include the prevention of marine pollution. The Authority shall have all the powers necessary for the attainment of its objectives. These shall include the power to regulate the manufacture, possession, use, sale and purchase of any vessel used for marine transport (sect. 7). The Minister may, by regulations, waive the application in whole or in part of this proclamation to small vessels.
Keywords: marine pollution; pollution control; pollution control; marine pollution; navigation; institution; governance

Title: Pesticide Registration and Control Council of State Decree (No. 20/1990).
Abstract: No person may manufacture, import, sell or use a pesticide not registered in accordance with this Special Decree. Notwithstanding registration, a pesticide may not be imported, stored, transported or offered for sale where not packed or labeled as provided in this Special Decree and directives issued hereunder. Application for the registration of a pesticide shall be made by the manufacture or by the importer in the form prescribed by the Minister. The Minister may, subject to such conditions as he thinks fit to impose, authorize registration upon satisfaction that the application complies with certain specified requirements. The Ministry shall keep a List of Registered Pesticides and issue a certificate of registration. Any package shall be designed and made in such a way that it contains the pesticide safely during transportation, storage, marketing, distribution and, use, including reuse where applicable, and in accordance with relevant standards set by the Ethiopian Standards Authority. Pesticides shall be labeled, transported and stored in accordance with provisions of this Decree. A Pesticide Advisory Committee is established. Inspectors may be appointed by the Minister. (29 sections)
Keywords: pesticides; institution; registration; inspection; packaging/labelling; transport/storage; institution; plant protection; governance

Title: Tigray National Regional State's Rural Land Usage Proclamation No. 23/1997.
Domain: Agricultural & rural dev.; Land & soil; Water
Abstract: This Proclamation lays down rules relative to the ownership and use of land in the National State of Tigray. Land is declared to be ”joint property” of the State and can not be sold, exchanged, given in lease or as bond for an indefinite time. Farmers may use land in their possession under conditions as set out in this Proclamation. The actual state of land is declared to be ”accepted” under the present Proclamation. Farmers can give their land in lease under article 7. Article 8 concerns the lease of state land. Article 9 contains rules relative the cultivation and either use of land, whereas article 10 concerns the growing of trees on cultivated land. Land will be administered by Councils at all levels in accordance with article 11. Article 16 deals with inheritance. Grazing shall be carried out in accordance with tradition and provisions laid down in article 18. Article 19 finally provides for usage relating to the use of water form water reservoirs, whether natural or constructed.
Keywords: farming; agricultural development; agricultural land; land reform; land tenure; traditional rights/customary rights; institution; ownership; governance; property rights; irrigation; servitude

Title: Maritime Code of the Empire of Ethiopia.
Abstract: A Law to provide for the nationality and registration of ships in Ethiopia, use of Ethiopian ships, and navigation in Ethiopian waters. The provisions of this Code are divided into 9 Titles: Ships (I); Shipowners, managers and the master (II); Regulation of maritime employment (III). Contracts relating to the use of the ship (IV); Maritime collisions, assistance, and salvage (V); Participation in general average (VI); Insurance (VII); Penal provisions (VIII); Miscellaneous. Articles 4 to 6 deal with the nationality of ships, i.e. specify criteria for the qualification as Ethiopian ship or for owning an Ethiopian ship. Remaining provisions of Title I deal with ownership of ships and rights on ships and the registration of ships in registers kept at every Ethiopian port. Article 46 concerns marking of ships.
Keywords: navigation; registration

Title: Settlement Authority Establishment Proclamation No. 78/1976.
Abstract: An autonomous public authority is established to take care of persons that have little or no land, the utilization of idle lands, the alleviation of unemployment, and the conservation of forest, soil and water resources in consultation with appropriate Government agencies. Powers and duties of the Authority are set out in section 6. The Authority shall have a Board consisting of specified ministers and a General Manager, the duties of which are set out in section 11. Section 13 specifies criteria for eligibility for the benefits of the settlement programme. Settlement shall take on unoccupied lands and on lands indicated by the Authority under section 13 with the consent of the Government.
Keywords: land reform; institution; abandoned land/unoccupied land; governance; land tenure

Title: Relief and Rehabilitation Commission Establishment Proclamation No. 173/1979.
Abstract: An autonomous public authority is established to co-ordinate relief activities and distribute relief aid, for the rehabilitation of people that are affected by disaster, to prevent future disasters, and to organize settlers in settlement areas. ”Disaster” here means flood, drought, earthquake, etc. Powers and duties of the Commission are set out in section 8, whereas special powers are defined in section 9. The Commission shall have a Council the powers of which are set out in section 13 and a Commissioner and two Deputy Commissioners.
Keywords: hazards; institution; governance

Title: State Farms Development Authority Proclamation No. 142/1978.
Abstract: An autonomous public authority is established under section 3. This Authority shall be in charge of the overall direction, supervision and co-ordination of the management and operation of agricultural development organizations established by the Authority pursuant to this Proclamation (‘corporations’), shall draw up a coordinated common plan for all corporations, ensure efficient function of the corporations and carry out studies requires to establish agro-industrial complexes. Powers and duties of the Authority are set out in section 6. The Authority shall have a General Manager, the duties of which are set out in section 8.
Keywords: agricultural development; institution; policy/planning; governance

Title: Agricultural Development Corporations Regulations No. 60/1978.
Abstract: These Rules shall apply to agricultural development organizations established by the Authority pursuant to the State Farms Development Authority Proclamation of 1978 (‘corporations’). It provides for juridical personality of corporations, capital and liability, powers and duties of each corporation, powers and duties of the General Manager of each corporation, keeping of books and accounts, budgeting, report of activities, reserve funds, auditing, dissolution, winding up and amalgamation of corporations.
Keywords: agricultural development; institution; policy/planning; governance

Title: Water Supply and Sewerage Authority Establishment Proclamation No. 219/1981.
Abstract: An autonomous public authority is established under section 3. This Authority shall be in charge of providing water supply and sewerage services throughout Ethiopia. The Authority shall be involved in the construction and maintenance of waterworks, control of supply of water and sewerage services by others and propose and submit to the National Water Resources Commission water tariffs and other charges and directives for the efficient organization of water and sewerage services. The Authority shall have a General Manager, the duties of which are set out in section 9.
Keywords: water resources management; institution; waterworks; water supply; sewerage; basic legislation; governance

Title: Municipal Public Health Rules 1950 issued with regard to water (10/1, 1950).
Abstract: No person shall offer to the public water for drinking purposes that is unsafe or water from an unsafe source, or water from a source that is in the opinion of a municipal public health officer liable to become unsafe. ”Unsafe” water is defined in rule 2. No person shall pollute public places as described in rule 3 or 4. No person shall discharge sewage water into natural water courses crossing town except as under a permit issued by the municipal public health officer or other specified officers. “Sewage is defined in rule 5. No person shall discharge sewage water into cesspools or abandoned wells or otherwise pollute natural groundwater at a depth of twelve meters of more (rule 6).
Keywords: pollution control; freshwater pollution; groundwater; sewerage

Title: Municipal Public Health Rules 1950 issued with regard to refuse.
Abstract: These Rules concern the handling of garbage by persons, shops and establishments, including waste from food. It prescribes the manner of storage of waste and prohibits the accumulation upon premises of any material that may attract breed flies.
Keywords: pollution control; waste disposal; waste prevention; waste management

Title: Council of Ministers Regulations to provide for the dissolution of the Tea Development and Marketing Enterprise (No. 31/1998).
Abstract: The Tea Development and Marketing Enterprise established by Council of Ministers Regulation No. 152 of 1993 is hereby dissolved. Rights and obligations of the Enterprise shall be transferred to the following enterprises: the Tea Production and Marketing Enterprise established by Regulations No. 28/1998; the Wush Wush Tea Development Enterprise established by Regulations No. 30/1998; and Tea Production and Marketing Enterprise established by Regulations No. 28/1998.
Keywords: plant production; institution; coffee/cocoa/tea; governance

Title: Council of Ministers Regulations to provide for the establishment of the Tea Production and Marketing Enterprise (No. 28/1998).
Abstract: There is hereby established the Tea Production and Marketing Enterprise as a public enterprise in the sense of the Public Enterprise Proclamation No. 25/1992. This enterprise shall be engaged in the processing of tea and the marketing of processed tea and shall carry out other activities related to those mentioned. The enterprise shall have a head office in Addis Ababa and may establish branch offices. A Supervising Authority of the enterprise shall be designated by the Government. (9 articles)
Keywords: institution; coffee/cocoa/tea; processing/handling; beverages; governance

Title: Council of Ministers Regulations to provide for the establishment of the Wush Wush Tea Development Enterprise (No. 30/1998).
Abstract: There is hereby established the Wush Wush Tea Development Enterprise as a public enterprise in the sense of the Public Enterprise Proclamation No. 25/1992. This enterprise shall be engaged in the development of tea plantations and the preliminary processing of tea and shall carry out other activities related to those mentioned. The enterprise shall have a head office in Wush Wush and may establish branch offices. A Supervising Authority of the enterprise shall be designated by the Government. (9 articles)
Keywords: institution; coffee/cocoa/tea; processing/handling; beverages; governance

Title: Council of Ministers Regulations to provide for the establishment of the Gumaro Tea Development Enterprise (No. 29/1998).
Abstract: There is hereby established the Gumaro Tea Development Enterprise as a public enterprise in the sense of the Public Enterprise Proclamation No. 25/1992. This enterprise shall be engaged in the development of tea plantations and the preliminary processing of tea and shall carry out other activities related to those mentioned. The enterprise shall have a head office in Gumaro and may establish branch offices. A Supervising Authority of the enterprise shall be designated by the Government. (9 articles)
Keywords: plant production; institution; coffee/cocoa/tea; governance

Title: Rural Land Administration Proclamation of the Federal Government of Ethiopia (No. 89/1997).
Abstract: This basic piece of legislation sets out principles and lays the foundations for laws relative to land tenure and administration of rural land are to be enacted by Regional Councils in respect of each Region of Ethiopia and in accordance with the present Proclamation, laws on environmental protection and land utilization policies. (Rural) land is declared to be a common property of the “Nations, Nationalities and Peoples” of Ethiopia and it is prescribed that land shall not be subject to sale or other means of exchange. Article 6 prescribes contents of the laws to be enacted, including matters such as assignment of land rights, demarcation of land, grazing, forestry and communal use. Regional governments shall determine rates of land-use fees and royalties on the use of forest resources.
Keywords: basic legislation; land tenure; land reform; public land; right of use; gender

Title: Ethiopian Seed Council of Ministers Regulations (No. 16/1997).
Abstract: These Regulations shall apply to any of the prescribed seeds of any designed variety of any plant species as may be specified by the Seed Industry Council established by Proclamation 35 of 1993. They shall not apply to seed grown by a farmer and sold directly to another farmer (art. 3). A new variety shall be approved, named and registered in accordance with these Regulations only when such variety conforms terms and conditions prescribed by the National Variety Release Committee. Producers, importers, processors or distributors of prescribed seeds shall be registered by the National Seed Industry Agency in accordance with article 5 and keep records in accordance with section 6. Quality control shall be carried out by the Ethiopian Authority for Standardization in accordance with article 7. Article 8 concerns labeling requirements. Sale of prescribed seeds requires a seed seller’s work permit (art. 9). Articles 10 to 16 concern the certification, sampling testing and inspection of prescribed seed. External trade in seeds shall be carried out only by registered importers and exporters. The Agency may designate certain seed as restricted seed, i.e. seed the importation or exportation of which is prohibited or restricted. The Council may issue Directives for the proper execution of these Regulations in regard of matters specified in article 19. (21 articles)
Keywords: breeders' rights; certification; plant variety; institution; registration; inspection; international trade; intellectual property rights; governance

Title: Quality and Standards Authority of Ethiopia Establishment Proclamation (No. 102/1998).
Abstract: The Quality and Standards Authority is re-established as an autonomous Federal Government Organ that shall be accountable to the Prime Minister. Its objectives shall be to assist and promote in the establishment of quality management practices and to issue standards. The Authority shall carry out duties as specified in article 6. The Authority shall be managed by a Board and shall have a General Manager. The Authority shall establish a national Conformity Assessment System, i.e. a method of determining directly or indirectly if relevant requirements are met. (19 articles)
Keywords: food safety and quality; hygiene/sanitary procedures; institution; standards; governance

Title: Animal, Animal Products and By-products Marketing Development Authority Establishment Proclamation (No. 117/1998).
Abstract: The Animal, Animal Products and By-products Marketing Development Authority is established as an autonomous Federal Government Organ that shall be accountable to the Prime Minister. The Authority shall promote the marketing of animals, animal products and by-products in Ethiopia and abroad, by increasing supply and quality of the items concerned. Article 6 imposes a vast range of duties on the Authority such as to preparation of laws, regulations and policies, to issue quality control directives, to establish staging points and quarantine stations, carry out research, supervise the construction of animal processing plants, etc. The Authority shall be managed by a Board and a Manager. Powers and duties of the Board and the Manager are defined in articles 10 and 11. The Council of Ministers may issue Regulations for the implementation of this Proclamation
Keywords: animal production; animal by-products; institution; quarantine; animal health; governance; meat; international trade; internal trade; institution; inspection; food safety and quality; governance

Title: Animal, Animal Products and By-products Marketing Development Authority Establishment (Amendment) Proclamation (No. 198/2000).
Abstract: The principal text is amended by changing the name of the Animal, Animal Products and By-products Marketing Development Authority in the Livestock Marketing Authority and by replacing the definition of “animal” with the definition of “livestock” so as to include animals, animal products and by-products in the definition. The duties regarding employment of staff of the Board and the Manager are extended.
Keywords: institution; governance; institution; governance

Title: Institute of Biodiversity Conservation and Research Establishment Proclamation (No. 120/1998).
Abstract: The Institute of Biodiversity Conservation and Research is established as an autonomous Federal Government Organ that shall be accountable to the Ethiopian Agricultural Research Organization. The objective of the Institute shall be to cause and ensure the appropriate conservation, research, development and sustainable utilization of the biodiversity of Ethiopia. “Biodiversity” is here defined as “the variability among living organisms, including plants, animals and microorganisms, and the ecological complexes of which they are part and this includes diversity within species (genes), between species and ecosystems” (art. 2). Powers and duties of the Institute are outlined in article 6. It shall propose legislation and policies, explore and survey biodiversity, be responsible for conservation of the country’s biological resources, coordinate conservation and research programmes, carry out re-stocking of local races, enrich Ethiopia’s biodiversity through other means, implement international conventions, conduct research on ecosystems, develop regional and international cooperation, etc. The Authority shall be managed by a General Manager. Powers of the Manager are defined in article 9. Supervision of the Institute is entrusted to Ethiopian Agricultural Research Organization Board. Its powers and duties are outlined in article 8.
Keywords: biodiversity; institution; ecosystem conservation; governance

Title: Awash Basin Water Resources Administration Agency Establishment Proclamation (No. 129/1998).
Abstract: The Awash Basin Water Resources Administration Agency is established as an autonomous Federal Government Organ that shall be accountable to the Minister of Water Resources. The objectives of the Agency shall be to co-ordinate, administer, allocate and regulate the utilization of the surface water resources of the Awash River Basin. The Agency shall administer the available water of the Basin that flows through territories of more than one Regional Government, construct waterworks, allocate water, implement improved water management methods, monitor groundwater level, construct and regulate irrigation and drainage works, dams, control gates, etc. The Authority shall be managed by a Board and a General Manager. Powers and duties of the Board and the Manager are defined in articles 9 and 11.
Keywords: inland waters; institution; monitoring; surface water; water supply; waterworks; river basin institution; irrigation; groundwater; basin/catchment/watershed; governance

Title: Fertilizer Manufacturing and Trade Proclamation (No. 137/1998).
Abstract: The 30 articles of this Proclamation are divided into 5 Sections: General (1); Competence Assurance Certificate (2); Manufacturing, dealing and distribution of fertilizer (3); Enforcement of bodies and their duties (4); Miscellaneous (5). A person who wants to engage in the wholesale or retail trade in, and importation, exportation or manufacturing of fertilizer (defined in article 20 shall hold a competence assurance certificate issued by the National Fertilizer Industry Agency. Articles 4 to 12 prescribe procedures of application and conditions for granting or renewal of a certificate. All fertilizers traded in Ethiopia shall be conform the requirements of Ethiopian standards and shall be registered by the Agency for use in Ethiopia as fertilizer (art. 13). Other provisions of Section Three concern package and labeling of fertilizer, sale of bulk fertilizers, sale of fertilizers that do not meet Ethiopian Standards, Notifications by importers, licensing of manufacturers, importers and traders, and disposal of adultered fertilizer. Section 4 defines duties and responsibilities of the National Fertilizer Industry Agency and the Quality and Standards Authority of Ethiopia in respect of matters covered by this Proclamation. The Authority shall inspect and certify imported fertilizer. The Agency shall carry out functions listed in article 22 in addition to those assigned to it by the Proclamation providing for the establishment of the Agency.
Keywords: fertilizers/nutrients; institution; international trade; packaging/labelling; inspection; authorization/permit; basic legislation; plant production; governance

Title: Cooperative Societies Proclamation (No. 147/1998).
Abstract: The text consists of 60 articles divided into 10 Parts: General (1); Formation and registration of cooperative societies (2); Rights and duties of members of a society (3); management bodies (4); Special privileges (5); Asset and funds societies (6); Audit and inspection (7); Dissolution and winding up of societies (8); Settlement of disputes (9); Miscellaneous provisions (10). “Cooperative societies” shall include, amongst others, agricultural cooperative societies and fishery cooperative societies. Article 4 defines the objectives of a society, whereas article 5 outlines the guiding principles of a cooperative society. Cooperative societies may, according to their nature, be established at different levels, i.e. from primary up to deferral level (art. 6). Societies shall be registered by appropriate authority (art. 9). Societies shall have juridical personality and issue proper by-laws (arts. 10 and 11). Articles 46 to 52 concern mediation and arbitration of disputes specified in article 9.
Keywords: basic legislation; cooperative/producer organization; non-governmental entity; agricultural development; dispute settlement

Title: National Veterinary Institute Establishment Council of Ministers Regulations (No. 52/1992).
Abstract: The National Veterinary Institute is established a s a public enterprise and as such shall be governed by the Public Enterprise Proclamation No. 52/1992. The Government shall designate a body to supervise the Institute. The purposes of the Institute are to produce vaccines of international standard for various animal diseases, to produce various veterinary drugs, “biologicals” and reagents and to sell such products locally and abroad. (9 articles)
Keywords: vaccination; drugs; institution; animal health; governance

Title: Ethiopian Water Resources Management Proclamation (No. 197/2000).
Abstract: The purpose of this Proclamation is to ensure that all surface and ground waters of Ethiopia are properly protected and managed. The text consists of 33 articles divided into 9 Parts: General provisions (1); Supervising body (2); Inventory of water resources and registry of actions (3); Permits and professional licenses (4); Fees and water charges (5); Servitude (6); Water banks and harmful effect of water (7); Association of water users (8); Transitory provisions (9). All water resources of Ethiopia are declared common property (art. 5). Article 6 sets out the fundamental principles of water management and administration. Use of water for domestic purposes shall have priority over all other water uses. Article 8 sets out the powers and duties of the Supervising Body, i.e. the Ministry of Water Resources at national level or any other organ delegated by the Ministry pursuant to comma 2 of article 8. The Supervising Body shall prepare or cause to be prepared an inventory of water resources in accordance with article 10. Supply of water, transfer of water, release or discharge of water or construction of waterworks requires a permit to be issued by the supervising Body in accordance with articles 11 to 18. Article 12 lists water uses for which no permit is required. The Supervising Body mat promote creation of water user’s associations and shall issue further Regulations regarding such associations (art. 27). (33 sections)
Keywords: framework law; basic legislation; water resources management; institution; groundwater; surface water; authorization/permit; dispute settlement; servitude; water supply; irrigation; water users' associations; servitude; comparative analysis; water rights; governance

Title: Research and Conservation of Cultural Heritage Proclamation (No. 209/2000).
Abstract: “Cultural heritage” is defined in article 2. The Authority for Research and Conservation of Cultural Heritage is established under article 2 as a government institution with a juridical personality. The Authority shall carry out scientific registration and supervision of cultural heritage, protect cultural heritage, etc. (art. 4). Powers and duties of the Authority are set out in article 6. The Authority shall have an Advisory Council and a General Manager. Powers and duties of the Council are set out in article 9, whereas powers of the General Manager are set out in article 11. Articles 29 and following concern exploration, discovery and study of cultural heritage. The Council of Ministers may declare reserved areas under section 42. )
Keywords: cultural heritage; institution; governance

Title: Emergency Food Security Reserve Administration Establishment Council of Ministers Regulations (No. 67/2000).
Abstract: An Emergency Food Reserve and a Non-Food Relief Items Reserve shall be maintained in accordance with articles 3 to 6. The Emergency Food Security Reserve Administration is established under article 7. It shall be accountable to the Disaster Prevention and Preparedness Commission. The Administration shall administer the Reserve, store and release food to meet food shortage and carry out other tasks set out in article 8. The Administration shall consist of a Food Security Reserve Board, an Emergency Food Security Reserve Technical Committee, a Manager and the necessary organizational structure and manpower. Powers and duties of the Board are set out in article 12. Powers and duties of the Technical Committee are set out in article 15. (21 articles)
Keywords: food security; institution; policy/planning; hazards; governance

Title: Ethiopian Agricultural Sample Enumeration Commission Establishment Proclamation (No. 238/2001).
Abstract: The Commission here established shall carry out agricultural census activities. It shall be accountable to the Council of Ministers. There shall be a Central Commission chaired by the Prime Minister and Regional and Zonal and other local Commissions. Section 11 sets out duties and powers of the Central Statistical Authority.
Keywords: agricultural development; access-to-information; institution; data collection/reporting; governance

Title: Re-enactment of the Urban Lease Holding Proclamation (No. 272/2002).
Abstract: A Proclamation to provide for the utilization of urban land. Urban land is defined as all land within urban boundaries (art. 2). The Proclamation shall apply to urban land held by a permit system, or by lease-hold system, as well as by other means in force prior to those systems (art. 3). Urban land may be held in long-term lease by permit in accordance with plan guidelines, on auction or through negotiation on the basis of a decision of the Region or city concerned (art. 4). A leasehold deed shall be conferred upon a person who is permitted to hold land on lease. Article 6 prescribes the duration of leases in various areas and for various uses. The rates of rent shall be determined by a law issued by the appropriate regional or city government (art. 8). A person to whom lease-hold of urban land is permitted shall begin use of the land in accordance with the permit within a period prescribed in Regulations issued by the regional or city government (art. 12). Article 15 provides for the termination of lease agreements. (25 sections)
Keywords: land tenure; urban land; lease; authorization/permit; contracts

Title: Cooperatives Commission Establishment Proclamation (No. 274 of 2002).
Abstract: This Proclamation provides for the establishment and functioning of a Commission that shall promote cooperative organization. The Commission shall be an autonomous Federal Government Organ and shall be accountable to the Ministry of Rural Development. The Commission shall formulate policies and prepare draft legislation, encourage organization of cooperative societies in line with international principles, carry out training and research, promote cooperative principles, organize, register and grant licences to cooperative societies and, audit and inspect societies and carry out other functions specified in article 5. There shall be a Commissioner who shall be the Chief Executive of the Commission.
Keywords: cooperative/producer organization; institution; agricultural development; governance

Title: Animal Diseases Prevention and Control Proclamation (No. 267 of 2002).
Domain: Livestock; Food & nutrition; Fisheries; Wild species & ecosystems
Abstract: A Proclamation to provide for the prevention and control of diseases affecting animals. ) Animal means for the purpose of this proclamation domestic and wild animals includs sea animals and bees. The text consists of 24 articles divided into 5 Parts: General Provisions (1); Prevention and control of animal diseases (2); Movement of animals, animal products and by-products (3); Registration of animal health professionals and delivery of services (4); Miscellaneous provisions (5). The Part 2 prescribes various measures relating to prevention of animal diseases and prevention of spreading of diseases such as notification of outbreak of a disease (art. 3), declaration of infected areas (art. 4), quarantine in infected areas (art. 5), prohibition of importation of animals, control of movement, control of diseases that may also affect wild animals or diseases of wild animals that may affect livestock, emergency preparedness, etc. (art. 8), exchange of health information (art. 9). Powers of Animals Health Officers are set out in article 8. Article 10 of Part 3 concerns establishment of quarantine stations, whereas article 14 concerns international health certificates. Importation of animals or products shall require an entrance permit from the Ministry of Agriculture.
Keywords: basic legislation; animal health; pests/diseases; institution; quarantine; international trade; inspection; pastoralism; certification; animal production; governance; fish diseases; animal health; meat; international trade; food safety and quality; animal health

Title: Water Resources Development Fund Establishment and its Administration Proclamation (No. 268 of 2002).
Abstract: The Proclamation provides for the establishment of the Water Resources Development Fund (art. 3), its objectives (art. 4), resources of the Fund (arts. 5 and 6) and administration of the Fund (arts. 9 to 18). The Fund shall be used to implement the objectives of this Proclamation. Those are enabling organizations that are engaged in water supply and sanitation services (defined in art. 2) to be fully self sufficient in the provision of reliable and sustainable services, to contribute to food self-sufficiency by expanding and ensuring water supply for irrigation. The Fund shall also provide long-term loans on the principle of cost recovery for the realization of the objectives. The Fund shall be managed by the Water Resources Development Fund Office established under article 9. The Office shall have a Board and a General Manager.
Keywords: agricultural development; food sovereignty; irrigation; water resources management; institution; special fund; irrigation; governance; credit; hygiene/sanitary procedures; water supply

Title: Ethiopian Rural Energy Development and Promotion Center Establishment Proclamation (No. 269 of 2002).
Abstract: This Proclamation provides for the establishment and functioning of a Center that shall create conditions for the development and promotion of rural energy resources and technology. “Energy” here means power generated from biomass, water, geothermal, sunlight, wind and non-renewable resources such as petroleum and minerals and various materials used in rural communities. The Center shall identify resources of energy suitable for rural areas, conduct studies for their development, adopt foreign technologies and develop indigenous energy technologies, provide consulting services, and carry out other functions outlined in article 5. The Center shall be managed by a Director General.
Keywords: energy conservation/energy production; institution; research; governance

Title: National Agricultural Input Authority Establishment Proclamation (No. 288 of 2002).
Abstract: This Proclamation provides for the establishment and functioning of an Authority that shall ensure that the production, supply, distribution and marketing of agricultural inputs (i.e. plant seeds, fertilizer, pesticides) is undertaken an efficient manner. The Authority shall be an autonomous Federal Government Organ and shall be accountable to the Ministry of Rural Development. Its duties include formulation of policies, issuance of importation and exportation permits, implementation of laws relating to agricultural inputs, etc. (art. 6). The Authority shall be managed by a General Manager, the powers and duties of which are outlined in article 8.
Keywords: agricultural development; institution; governance; pesticides; seeds/planting material; fertilizers/nutrients; institution; international trade; agricultural development; plant production; plant protection; governance

Title: Environmental Protection Organs Establishment Proclamation (No. 295 of 2002).
Abstract: This Proclamation provides for the re-establishment and functioning of an Environmental Protection Authority as an autonomous Federal Government Organ and shall be accountable to the Prime Minister. The Authority shall have as objective the formulation of policies, strategies, laws and standards that foster social of economic development in an environmentally sustainable manner (art. 5). The Authority shall formulate and coordinate environmental policies, establish a system for environmental impact assessment, review impact assessment reports, set environmental standards, carry out environmental auditing, carry out studies and research in the field of desertification prepare directives for the implementation of environmental laws, coordinate measures for the implementation of national environment objectives, and carry out other functions specified in article 6. The Authority shall be managed by a Director General and a Council (“Environmental Council”). Every Competent Agency (defined in article 2) shall establish or designate an environmental unit that shall be responsible for coordination and follow-up so that the activities of the Agency concerned are in conformity wit this Proclamation and other environmental legislation. In each Regional State Regional Environmental Agencies shall be established in accordance with article 15. (17 articles)
Keywords: institution; pollution control; environmental planning; policy/planning; governance

Title: Environmental Impact Assessment Proclamation (No. 299 of 2002).
Abstract: This Proclamation prescribes that no person shall commence any new development activity under any category listed in any directive issued pursuant to this Proclamation ('project') which requires an environmental impact assessment (further specified in art. 5) without an authorization of the Environmental Protection Authority. The Authority or the relevant regional environmental agency may decide that the possible impact of the project is significant and therefore that no EIA shall be carried out (art. 3). Licensing agencies shall before issuing an investment permit or trade or operating license, ensure that EIA requirements have been fulfilled. Article 4 sets out criteria for the determination of impact. Article 6 concerns impact assessment for projects that are likely to have an impact on the environment of two or more regions. Proponents shall draft IEA in accordance with articles 7 to 9. The Authority shall take a decision on the submitted project/EIA in accordance with article 9. Other provisions of this Proclamation deal with occurrence of new circumstance (art. 11), monitoring of implementation (art. 12), EIA of a public instrument (art. 13), jurisdiction of agencies (art. 14), public participation (art. 15), and various miscellaneous issues. Article 18 prescribes offences and penalties.
Keywords: institution; pollution control; environmental impact assessment (EIA); basic legislation; cultural heritage; sustainable development; governance; freshwater pollution; pollution control

Title: Environmental Pollution Control Proclamation (No. 300 of 2002).
Abstract: The Proclamation consists of 22 articles divided into 6 Parts: Preliminary (1); Control of pollution (2); Environmental standards (3); Environmental inspectors (4); Offences and penalties (5); Miscellaneous provisions (6). Article 3 sets out general rules regarding control or prevention of pollution including use of clean technologies and the polluter pays principle. Article 4 concerns hazardous waste, chemical substances and radioactive substance. Article 5 provides for collection, transportation, treatment (including recycling) of municipal waste. The Environmental Protection Authority shall formulate “practicable” environmental standards based on scientific and environmental principles. The standards shall at least have respect to: discharge or effluent waste water and sewerage, air quality, subsoil, noise and waste management (art. 6). Environmental Inspectors shall be nominated by the Authority or the Regional Environmental Agency. Powers and duties of the Inspectors are set out in article 8. Inspectors may order remedial action in case any activity causes damage to the environment. Appeal against decisions of Inspectors may be had under article 9.
Keywords: framework law; pollution control; institution; governance; freshwater pollution; effluent waste water/discharge; pollution control; waste management; waste prevention; effluent waste water/discharge; hazardous waste; inspection; recycling/reuse; offences/penalties

Title: Fisheries Development and Utilization Proclamation (No. 315/2003).
Abstract: The objectives of this Proclamation are to conserve fish biodiversity and its environment, to avoid over-exploitation of fish resources, to increase the supply of fish of good quality and to expand the development of aquaculture. The 21 articles of this Proclamation are divided into 4 Parts: General (1); Fisheries Resource Utilization (2); Enforcement of this Proclamation (3); Miscellaneous provisions (4). Commercial fishing requires a legal fishing permit. Specific permits are also required for fishing in national parks or reserved fishing areas, protected fishing areas, and recreational fishing by non-nationals. The permits cannot be transferred. Fishing in an area that is subject to a concession granted under article 7 shall require a permit from the concession holder. Other provisions of article 5 concerns permits for the international trade in exotic fish, transfer of live fish, prohibition of illegal fishing methods and permits for fisheries research. Article 6 concerns regulation of aquaculture and the prevention of fish diseases. Article 8 concerns protection of the environment, whereas article 9 deals with transboundary and transregional fisheries resources. Handling, processing storage, transportation and trade of fish and fish product shall meet fish quality and trade standards and be in conformity with Regulations issued under this Proclamation (art. 10).
Keywords: fishery management and conservation; inland fisheries; aquaculture; concession; fish diseases; offences/penalties; fishing authorization; animal health; authorization/permit; ecosystem conservation; biodiversity

Title: Seed Proclamation No. 206 of 2000.
Abstract: This Proclamation, consisting of 37 sections divided into five Parts, introduces rules and measures to ensure production and availability of high quality seeds for agricultural and horticultural purposes in Ethiopia. It creates a legal framework for the protection and control of the interests of users of seed, originators, processors and traders of seed. The Proclamation shall apply to any seed prescribed by the National Seed Industry Agency (sect. 3). Section 5 requires any person engaging in seed production or trade to obtain a Competence Assurance Certificate from the Agency. The holder of such certificate shall keep records and samples of seed in accordance with section 13. Sections 14 to 24 concern the control of quality of seed production and marketing and provide for seed quality control according to appropriate standards by the Agency, labelling of seed, certification of seed by the Agency or another delegated body, recognition of foreign certification bodies, testing of seed and inspection of seeds. Section 25 contains rules relative to the importation and exportation of seeds. Sections 29 to 31 define the role of the Agency and the National Variety Release Committee in the control of the production and marketing of seeds. Section 34 defines offences and prescribes penalties.
Keywords: seeds/planting material; certification; plant variety; institution; authorization/permit; inspection; international trade; offences/penalties; plant production; governance

Title: Access to Genetic Resources and Community Knowledge, and Community Rights Proclamation  (No. 482/2006).
Abstract: This Proclamation, which has the force of Law, concerns the protection and enhancement of customary use of genetic resources by Ethiopian communities which are relevant to the conservation and sustainable use of the biodiversity resources of the country. It provides rules relative to the access to genetic resources and community knowledge on use of those genetic resources, and provides for the rights of communities over genetic resources and community knowledge in conformity with the Convention on Biological Diversity to which Ethiopia is a Party. The Proclamation shall apply to access to genetic resources found in in-situ or ex-situ conditions but shall not apply to customary use and exchange of genetic resources and the sale of produce of biological resources for direct consumption, that does not involve the use of the genetic resource thereof. The Proclamation defines ownership rights of genetic resources and community knowledge and provides for protection of community rights, access to genetic resources and sharing of benefits. Access to genetic resources by outsiders requires a permit to be granted by the Institute of Biological Conservation. The Proclamation also regulates the exploration of genetic resources and provides for administration in relation with the implementation of its provisions.
Keywords: basic legislation; genetic resources; plant production; seeds/planting material; plant variety; access-to-information; breeders' rights; access and benefit-sharing; PIC-prior informed consent; biodiversity; traditional knowledge/indigenous knowledge; authorization/permit; intellectual property rights; biodiversity; PIC-prior informed consent; traditional knowledge/indigenous knowledge; Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC); access right; authorization/permit; community management; data collection/reporting; genetic resources; hygiene/sanitary procedures; quarantine

Title: Plant Breeders' Rights Proclamation (No. 481/2006).
Abstract: This Proclamation, which has the force of Law, provides for the protection of rights of breeders in respect new plant varieties. The list of new plant genera and species shall be published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development and revised from time to time. A breeder shall be granted by the Ministry, on application, a plant breeders’ right in respect of his or her new plant variety. Subject to the exemptions and restrictions provided for in this Proclamation, a plant breeders’ right entitles the holder an exclusive right to: (a) sell, including the right to license other persons to sell, the seed or propagating material of the protected variety; and (b) produce, including the right to license other persons to produce, propagating material of the protected variety for sale. The Proclamation makes provision for the granting of compulsory licenses by the Ministry, provides with respect to application, registration, duration, revocation and transfer of a right, and to legal action in the case of infringement of a right. The Proclamation also sets out the principle of  a farmers’ right and defines such right.
Keywords: basic legislation; plant production; breeders' rights; genetic resources; seeds/planting material; plant variety; registration; authorization/permit; intellectual property rights

Title: Mining Operations Council of Ministers Regulations No. 182/1994.
Abstract: These Regulations of the Council of Ministers provide rules relative to large-scale and small-scale mining operations. The rules concern, among other things: (a) the issue, renewal or revocation of a prospecting licence or an exploration licence; (b) notice of discovery of minerals; (c) verification and certification of a discovery; (d) rights and obligations of licencees; (e) fees, royalties and other payments; (f) offences and sanctions; (g) dispute settlement; and (h) powers and duties of the Controller. The Controller, i.e. an officer appointed by the Licensing Authority to control mining operations, shall have the primary responsibility with regard to the technical and administrative supervision of mining operations in accordance with directives issued by Licensing Authority. “Mining” includes the abstraction of mineral water or thermal water. An application for a large-scale mining operation shall include an environmental assessment report and licences holders shall observe various rules regarding the protection of the environment.
Keywords: pollution control; soil rehabilitation; water abstraction; thermal and medicinal waters; mining; exploration; minerals; environmental impact assessment (EIA); dispute settlement; authorization/permit

Title: Regulations to amend the Mining Operations Council of Ministers Regulations (No. 27/1998).
Abstract: These Regulations amend the Mining Operations Regulations by deleting article 33 and renumbering articles 34 to 45. Article 33 concerns annual rentals to be paid by licensees.
Keywords: fees/royalties

Title: Mining Proclamation No.52/1993.
Abstract: This Proclamation lays down the regulatory framework for mining operations in Ethiopia. It defines the principles of sound development of the mining sector and defines the criteria for eligibility for mining rights, i.e. a prospecting licence, an exploration licence, an artisanal mining licence, a small-scale mining licence and a large-scale mining licence. A mining licence shall give the right to abstract, in limited quantities, mineral and geothermal water. Furthermore, the Proclamation defines the rights and duties of licence holders and provides for financial matters and administration. An applicant for a large-scale mining licence shall submit an environmental impact study before the granting of a licence.
Keywords: soil rehabilitation; waterworks; water abstraction; basic legislation; mining; exploration; minerals; environmental impact assessment (EIA); dispute settlement; authorization/permit

Title: Mining (Amendment) Proclamation No.22/1996.
Abstract: This Proclamation amends the Mining Proclamation in article 44 relative to a participation interest of the Government in large-scale mining investments and in article 46 relative to the competent authority for the grant of a licence.
Keywords: mining; exploration; authorization/permit

Title: Mining (Amendment) Proclamation No.118/1998.
Abstract: This Proclamation amends the Mining Proclamation in article 40 relative to rates for surface rentals and in article 46 relative to the power to issue licences and to collect royalties and other payments on large-scale mining operations.
Keywords: mining; exploration; fees/royalties; authorization/permit

Title: Petroleum Operations Proclamation No. 295/1986.
Abstract: This Proclamation sets out rules relative to operations involving and related to the exploration, development, extraction, production, treatment, storage, transportation and marketing of petroleum, excluding refining of crude oil, but including the processing of natural gas. The Proclamation defines powers of the Minister to regulate petroleum operations and to control contractors and it sets out particulars of a petroleum agreement to be concluded with a contractor. Both the particulars of the agreement and operating standards mention the obligation of a contractor to protect the environment. In additions, a contractor shall conduct petroleum operations in a manner designed to protect anthropological, archaeological and historical objects and sites.
Keywords: basic legislation; mining; exploration; oil; natural gas; contracts; authorization/permit

Title: Radiation Protection Proclamation No. 571/2008.
Abstract: This Proclamation seeks to reduce risks of damage to health, property and the environment due to use of radiation and radioisotopes, through proper and effective protection schemes. For this purpose, the Proclamation establishes Ethiopian Radiation Protection Authority, which shall regulate radiation sources and related practices. The Authority shall be managed by the Ethiopian Radiation Protection Board and shall have radiation protection officers to ensure compliance with the provisions of this Proclamation. The Authority shall, among other things, formulate radiation protection policies and legislation and issue licences under this Proclamation to mine, manufacture, construct, assemble, acquire, transit, import, stored, etc. a radioactive material. All such activities shall be notified to the Authority. The Proclamation furthermore, among other things, defines duties and responsibilities of licensees and other concerned parties and grants regulation-making powers for the implementation of provisions of this Proclamation to the Council of Ministers.
Keywords: radiation; institution; authorization/permit; pollution control; emissions; governance; pollution control; hazardous waste; waste management

Title: Transfer of Rights and Obligations of Disaster Prevention and Preparedness Commission to the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development Proclamation No. 593/2008.
Primary subjects: Agricultural & rural development; Disaster risk management
Abstract: This Proclamation repeals the Disaster Prevention and Preparedness Commission Establishment Proclamation No. 10/1995, as amended and transfers the rights and obligations of Disaster Prevention and Preparedness Commission established under Proclamation No.10/1995 to the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development.
Keywords: hazards; institution; governance

Title: Water Resources Development Fund Establishment and Administration (Amendment) Proclamation No. 581/2008.
Abstract: This Proclamation amends the Water Resources Development Fund Establishment and Its Administration Proclamation: adding definitions of ‘Institution’ and ‘Revolving Fund’; in article 4 in relation with tasks of the Fund; in article 5 in relation with determination of interest rates on loans provided by the Fund; in article 7 concerning criteria for eligibility to be a beneficiary of the Fund; and in article 11 relating to powers and duties of the Water Resources Development Fund Office.
Keywords: water resources management; institution; special fund; agricultural development; governance

Title: Coffee Quality Control and Marketing Proclamation No. 602/2008.
Abstract: This scope of this Proclamation is to establish an improved system for coffee quality control and marketing. The Proclamation provides rules relative to the coffee quality control process and rules relative to transactions involving coffee. In addition, it defines obligations of coffee producers, coffee traders and coffee exporters, defines powers of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development and defines offences.
Keywords: food safety and quality; coffee/cocoa/tea; international trade; institution; classification/declassification; certification; offences/penalties; beverages; governance; plant production; agricultural commodities

Title: Urban Planning Proclamation No. 574/2008.
Abstract: This Proclamation provides rules relative to spatial and development planning in urban centres in Ethiopia. It establishes a legal framework in order to promote planned and well developed urban centres and regulates and facilitates development activities in urban centres to enhance economic development of the country. An urban centre is defined as any locality with established municipality or having a population size of 2000 or above inhabitants, of which 50 percent of its labour force is primarily engaged in non-agricultural activities. Physical boundaries of urban centres shall be demarcated by regional authorities. A structure plan shall take into account environmental aspects, in particular Art. 11/3/f requires any local development plan to state, among others, green areas, open spaces, water bodies, and places that might be utilized for common benefits.  The Proclamation sets out the procedure for the adoption of plans including public hearings. It also provides for an  authorization of development, reallocation of land for public purposes, a stop that may be imposed on development by authorities, the right to obtain information regarding the status of land and the reservation of land for public purposes.
Keywords: land-use planning; urban land; institution; cultural heritage; governance; environmental planning; policy/planning

Title: Ethiopian Wildlife Development and Conservation Authority Establishment Proclamation No. 575/2008.
Abstract: This Proclamation establishes the Ethiopian Wildlife Development and Conservation Authority as an autonomous public agency of the federal government. The Authority shall, among other things: (a) prepare and submit to the Ministry of Culture and Tourism draft policies and laws relating to the development, conservation and utilization of wildlife resources and follow up the their implementation; (b) develop and administer wildlife conservation areas; (c) issue hunting permits to foreign tourists; (d) issue permits and health certificates to export and import any wildlife or wildlife products; (e) ensure that wildlife conservation areas are established in accordance with international standards with a view to facilitating their registration by the World Conservation Union.
Keywords: management/conservation; institution; hunting/capture; wildlife products; governance

Title: Disclosure and Registration of Assets Proclamation (No. 668/2010).
Abstract: This Proclamation requires (future) public servants to disclose to and register with the Federal Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission their interests in assets, including immovable property, so as to enhance transparency and accountability in the conduct of public affairs. Customary law shall not apply to matters provided for by this Proclamation. Any public office or public enterprise shall ensure compliance with this Proclamation.
Keywords: land tenure; ownership; offences/penalties; governance; property rights

Title: Food, Medicine and Health Care Administration and Control Proclamation No. 661/2009.
Domain: Livestock; Food & nutrition; Water; Waste & hazardous substances
Abstract: This Proclamation provides with respect to matters of public health in Ethiopia including health risks resulting from unsafe and substandard quality of food. In Particular, the Proclamation applies to, among other things: (a) setting standards in relation to food, medicine, environmental health: (b) the licensing and regulating trans-regional food and medicine production, import, export, distribution, promotion and storage of food and sampling and analysis of food; (c) monitoring and regulating environmental health services; (d) other regulatory activities with respect to trans-regional food, medicine, health and controllable health related services and institutions. The principal administrative authority for purposes of this Proclamation shall be the Executive Organ, i.e. a body to be established by Regulations of the Council of Ministers to implement food, medicine and healthcare administration and control activities at the federal level. Matters of food dealt with by this Proclamation include: food safety control; licensing of persons handling food; packaging and labelling; nutritional standards; importation and exportation of food; food irradiation; and quality control on water supplied to the public in bottle or through pipes. The Proclamation also makes provision with respect to waste handling and disposal and the storage of dangerous chemicals.
Keywords: animal health; drugs; basic legislation; food safety and quality; hygiene/sanitary procedures; institution; standards; treated food; mineral water; packaging/labelling; inspection; international trade; offences/penalties; governance; water supply; potable water; waste disposal; waste management; hazardous substances

Title: Apiculture Resources Development and Protection Proclamation (No. 660/2009).
Abstract: This Proclamation provides for the conservation of the biodiversity of honey bee races and honey source plants and the development of the apiculture and the production of honey products. The Proclamation provides rules for the authorization of beekeeping activities including migratory beekeeping and for the protection of indigenous honeybee species from communicable honeybee diseases. The Proclamation furthermore, among other things, provides some rules relative to importation of bees and bee products, provides for appointment and functions of apiculture resources development inspectors and defines offences.
Keywords: animal production; apiculture/sericulture; animal health; pests/diseases; international trade; authorization/permit; offences/penalties; biodiversity

Title: Biosafety Proclamation (No.655/2009).
Abstract: This Proclamation provides rules for the handling and use of Genetically Modified Organisms so as to protect human and animal health, biological diversity and in general, the environment, local communities and the country at large. It aims at preventing or at least managing down to levels of insignificance the adverse effects of modified organisms. No person shall engage in any transaction without obtaining an advance informed agreement from the Environmental Protection Authority, i.e. a written consent granted by the Authority for the undertaking of a transaction in accordance with this Proclamation. Title: River Basin Councils and Authorities Proclamation (No. 534/2007).
